ai_insights.executive_summary: The test executed 3,871 total samples across 18 journey iterations with 20 concurrent users over 235 seconds, achieving 16.45 req/s throughput. Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% (22 of 48 main transactions met targets), with 26 transactions violating NFR SLAs. Critical failures were driven by 100% error rates in 15 transactions and P90 latency breaches in 6 transactions, despite average response time being 164.11 ms due to successful transactions masking systemic failures.

findings.title: Universal Application Error Failure Across Critical User Journeys
findings.observation: Fifteen (15) main transactions exhibited 100% error rates (18/18, 17/17, etc. samples failed), including TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal, and all cart/checkout/update operations (TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart through TC04_T_09_Update_Cart_Quantities), directly causing journey-level failures in TC_02_Add_To_Cart (108/191 failed) and TC_04_User_Sign_In (84/192 failed).
findings.likely_cause: Application logic failure or misconfiguration preventing successful execution of core user flows, independent of load.
findings.why_it_matters: Core user journeys for browsing, cart operations, and authentication are completely broken, resulting in zero successful transactions for critical paths and direct revenue impact.
findings.recommendation: Immediately investigate application deployment, dependency availability (e.g., product catalog, cart service), and authentication service configuration. Validate with smoke tests in staging.
findings.validation: Run isolated functional tests for TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart and TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials to confirm fix before load testing.

findings.title: High Latency in Successful Launch and Authentication Transactions
findings.observation: Six (6) transactions with 0% error rates exceeded P90 SLA targets: TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage (P90=664ms vs 500ms target, +32.8%), TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal (P90=668ms, +33.6%), TC04_T_01_Launch_Authentication_Gateway (P90=666ms, +33.2%), TC02_T_01_Launch_Shopping_Catalog (P90=665ms, +33.0%), TC04_T_11_Perform_User_Sign_Out (P90=656ms, +31.2%), and TC03_T_11_Search_Nonexistent_Product (P90=563ms, +12.6%).
findings.likely_cause: Backend service slowness or database latency in product catalog and authentication systems under load, despite no application errors.
findings.why_it_matters: Users experience slow page loads for homepages, search, and login/logout flows, degrading experience even when transactions succeed, increasing bounce risk.
findings.recommendation: Profile database query performance and application server response times for product catalog and authentication endpoints. Implement caching for static category data and optimize login validation logic.
findings.validation: Monitor P90 latency for TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC04_T_01_Launch_Authentication_Gateway after optimization; target <500ms.

findings.title: Throughput and Latency Stabilize After Initial Ramp-Up, Indicating No Infrastructure Saturation
findings.observation: Throughput increased steadily from 0.8 req/s at 4 users (10s) to 3.9 req/s at 20 users (2m), then stabilized between 3.4-3.9 req/s for the remainder of the test. Average response time decreased from 669ms at 10s to 407-413ms range after 1m, with P95/P99 stabilizing at 560-575ms. No sustained increase in latency or error rate beyond initial ramp-up was observed.
findings.likely_cause: Application failure (not infrastructure limits) capped throughput; server resources were not saturated as latency did not grow with concurrency after stabilization.
findings.why_it_matters: Infrastructure scaling would not resolve the core issue; the system can handle higher load if application errors are fixed, as evidenced by stable latency at 20 users.
findings.recommendation: Focus remediation on application fixes rather than infrastructure scaling. Validate capacity by fixing error rates and re-running test to observe true throughput potential.
findings.validation: After fixing application errors, re-run test and verify throughput increases beyond 3.9 req/s with latency remaining stable.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: No infrastructure saturation point observed; latency and throughput stabilized after initial ramp-up, indicating application failure, not resource limits, capped performance.
capacity_planning.analysis: Throughput scaled linearly with concurrency during ramp-up (0.8 req/s at 4 users → 3.9 req/s at 20 users) and stabilized thereafter without latency growth or error spikes beyond initial period. Since 15 transactions had 100% error rates independent of load, the system's capacity is currently limited by application defects. Fixing these would allow true capacity assessment; until then, no safe concurrency can be recommended for successful transaction completion.

root_cause_assessment.finding: Universal application error failure in core user journeys
root_cause_assessment.evidence: Fifteen transactions showed 100% error rates (e.g., TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart: 17/17 errors, TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials: 17/17 errors), directly causing journey failures in TC_02_Add_To_Cart (108/191 failed) and TC_04_User_Sign_In (84/192 failed).
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Application logic failure, missing dependencies, or misconfiguration in cart, catalog, and authentication services.
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Check service logs for null pointer exceptions or dependency timeouts in cart and authentication modules. Validate product catalog and user service availability via direct API calls.

recommendations.title: Fix 100% Error Rate in Cart and Authentication Transactions
recommendations.why: Fifteen core transactions including cart operations (TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart) and login (TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials) failed 100% of the time, breaking all user journeys and preventing any successful checkouts or account actions.
action: Review application logs for TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart and TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials to identify exception stack traces.
Validate dependency availability (product inventory, user profile service) and configuration flags for cart and authentication modules.
recommendations.expected_impact: Restore successful execution of core user journeys, enabling measurable throughput and SLA compliance for cart, checkout, and authentication flows.
recommendations.validation: Re-run load test and verify error rate for TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart and TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials drops below 1% SLA threshold.

recommendations.title: Optimize High-Latency Successful Transactions in Launch and Auth Flows
recommendations.why: Six transactions with 0% error rates exceeded P90 SLA targets by up to 33.6% (TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal: 668ms vs 500ms), degrading user experience for homepage, search, and login/logout flows despite success.
action: Profile database queries and service call times for product catalog and authentication endpoints during TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC04_T_01_Launch_Authentication_Gateway.
Implement caching for static category data (e.g., fish, reptiles sections) and optimize login validation logic to reduce round trips.
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduce P90 latency for launch and authentication transactions to under 500ms, improving page load times and user retention.
recommendations.validation: After optimization, verify P90 latency for TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC04_T_01_Launch_Authentication_Gateway is ≤500ms in a follow-up load test.

executive_summary.assessment_text: The test revealed critical application failures preventing core user journeys, with 15 transactions failing 100% of the time and 6 successful transactions exceeding latency SLAs. Infrastructure showed no saturation as throughput stabilized and latency remained flat after ramp-up, indicating the system is limited by software defects, not capacity. Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% due to pervasive errors and tail latency in key paths.
assessment_bullets: Fifteen main transactions failed 100% of the time (e.g., TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart: 17/17 errors), breaking cart, checkout, and authentication journeys.
Throughput stabilized at 3.4-3.9 req/s after 1 minute with no latency growth, indicating no infrastructure saturation despite 20 concurrent users.
Six successful transactions exceeded P90 SLA by up to 33.6% (TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal: 668ms vs 500ms), degrading experience for homepage and search flows.
conclusions: Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% (22 of 48 main transactions met targets), with 26 transactions violating NFR SLAs due to errors or latency.
Total journey iterations: 18; TC_02_Add_To_Cart had 108 failed executions out of 191, TC_04_User_Sign_In had 84 failed out of 192.
Average response time was 164.11 ms, but this masks systemic failure as successful transactions were fast while critical paths failed entirely.
